clips.speaker: Rob Kaplan
clips.title: 高盛副主席卡普兰：新美联储主席的谨慎信号
title_lines: 新美联储主席的谨慎信号

subtitles.en: Joining us now from Dallas is Rob Kaplan, Goldman Sachs' vice chairman and former Dallas Fed president.
subtitles.zh: 现在连线达拉斯的罗伯·卡普兰，高盛副主席、前达拉斯联储主席。

subtitles.en: Rob, it's always great to have you on the program. A lot of us have not really heard too much and really know the new chairman here.
subtitles.zh: 罗伯，很高兴你上节目。我们很多人对新主席还不太了解。

subtitles.en: We learned that he's serious about not wanting to make predictions or give forward guidance.
subtitles.zh: 我们了解到他认真对待不做预测或前瞻指引。

subtitles.en: And he also learned that he's probably even gonna be careful about describing the Fed's reaction function.
subtitles.zh: 他还可能对描述美联储的反应函数非常谨慎。

subtitles.en: And then the last thing is, which was not surprising, there are four or five areas, and I think this is a good thing. He wants to review practices and that's why he's setting up these task forces.
subtitles.zh: 最后一点，不意外，有四五个领域，我认为这是好事。他想审查做法，所以设立这些工作组。

subtitles.en: And so we learned that he's serious about that, that the drawbacks of that approach or the adjustment the markets are having to make is he didn't really give a glimpse into the debate.
subtitles.zh: 所以我们了解到他对此很认真，这种方法的缺点或市场必须做出的调整是他没有透露辩论内容。

subtitles.en: The statement probably is the best guide you have and I'll make a comment on that.
subtitles.zh: 声明可能是你最好的指南，我会对此发表评论。

clips.speaker_context: Goldman Sachs vice chairman and former Dallas Fed president

clips.speaker: Rob Kaplan
clips.title: 高盛卡普兰：通胀与AI的拉锯战，美联储面临两难

subtitles.en: It's a tension between an infrastructure boom, CapEx AI-related, infrastructure-related data center boom in the US, which is probably inflationary and straining resources and labor.
subtitles.zh: 美国基础设施繁荣、AI相关资本支出、数据中心繁荣，这可能是通胀性的，并给资源和劳动力带来压力。

subtitles.en: At the same time over the horizon, we have an AI adoption boom coming, which should be disinflationary.
subtitles.zh: 同时，未来还有AI应用繁荣，这应该是通缩性的。

subtitles.en: And we have a war that has been negatively affecting prices that ideally is coming to an end and a straight being reopened.
subtitles.zh: 还有一场对价格产生负面影响的战争，理想情况下即将结束，海峡重新开放。

subtitles.en: And so that's kind of the balance that previous Fed shares would have described.
subtitles.zh: 这就是之前美联储主席会描述的平衡。

subtitles.en: And I think he's telling us, you're going to have to surmise that he's not going to take you through that debate.
subtitles.zh: 我认为他在告诉我们，你必须推测他不会带你经历这场辩论。
en_highlights: not going to take you through

clips.speaker_context: Goldman Sachs vice chairman and former Dallas Fed president

clips.speaker: Rob Kaplan
clips.title: 高盛卡普兰：通胀若持续，美联储9月前必须行动

subtitles.en: If the inflation prints over the summer don't cool a little bit, they can maybe wait past the July meeting, but I think if they don't cool by September, I think there's going to be a lot of pressure on the Fed to take action to deliver that promised price stability.
subtitles.zh: 如果夏季通胀数据没有稍微降温，他们可以等到7月会议之后，但如果到9月仍未降温，我认为美联储将面临很大压力，需要采取行动以实现承诺的价格稳定。

subtitles.en: I don't think that's a market pressure. I think that's a reality pressure.
subtitles.zh: 我不认为那是市场压力，我认为那是现实压力。

subtitles.en: So they've got some time, but I don't know that they have a lot of time beyond September.
subtitles.zh: 所以他们还有一些时间，但我不知道9月之后他们是否还有很多时间。

clips.speaker_context: Goldman Sachs vice chairman and former Dallas Fed president

clips.speaker: Rob Kaplan
clips.title: 高盛卡普兰：点阵图可能过时，市场需谨慎解读

subtitles.en: Well, here's the caution. And obviously I submitted a lot of these SCPs when I was at the Fed.
subtitles.zh: 这里要谨慎。显然我在美联储时提交了很多这样的SCP。

subtitles.en: You get it ready to submit by Thursday Friday of last week. It's announced over the weekend and clear the war is coming to an end. The straight is being reopened and you've already done all your work.
subtitles.zh: 你上周四、五准备好提交，周末宣布战争即将结束，海峡重新开放，而你已经完成了所有工作。

subtitles.en: And so could I imagine that if that dot plot was done six weeks from now, you won't get another one until September that it might be softer than the rate path than nine that are suggesting.
subtitles.zh: 所以我能想象，如果点阵图是在六周后做的，下一次要到9月，它可能比现在暗示的利率路径更温和。

subtitles.en: That's possible because you've got a lot changing right now. And if I were in my former seat, I would be urging caution about over interpreting this dot plot because we just had a big change.
subtitles.zh: 这有可能，因为现在很多事情在变。如果我在原来的位置，我会敦促谨慎解读这个点阵图，因为我们刚刚经历了一个重大变化。

subtitles.en: And so that's a caution on this and the market only is just reacting to the data it has.
subtitles.zh: 所以对此要谨慎，市场只是对现有数据做出反应。

subtitles.en: And I think it's worth noting that there ought to be a significant caution on interpreting this dot plot.
subtitles.zh: 我认为值得注意的是，解读这个点阵图应该非常谨慎。

clips.speaker_context: Goldman Sachs vice chairman and former Dallas Fed president

clips.speaker: Rob Kaplan
clips.title: 高盛卡普兰：若通胀顽固，9月加息或开启紧缩周期

subtitles.en: I mean, personally, if inflation prints don't cool between now and we get to September, I actually think the balance of risks suggested would be wise to take some action either in September or in the fall.
subtitles.zh: 我个人认为，如果从现在到9月通胀数据没有降温，风险平衡表明在9月或秋季采取行动是明智的。

subtitles.en: I think if inflation stays sticky, it tells me that the stance is accommodative and too accommodative and we need to take action.
subtitles.zh: 如果通胀持续顽固，这表明政策立场是宽松的，甚至过于宽松，我们需要采取行动。

subtitles.en: But that's why you have a debate around the table. You're going to have people who agree with that and you have people who disagree. His job is to orchestrate and referee that debate.
subtitles.zh: 但这就是为什么会有辩论。有人同意，有人不同意。他的工作是组织和主持这场辩论。

subtitles.en: There's a difference raw between perhaps an insurance hike and entering a tightening cycle. Which of the two do you think we're in?
subtitles.zh: 保险性加息和进入紧缩周期之间有本质区别。你认为我们处于哪种？

subtitles.en: So just if you go through history and I've been part of these in the past, it is unusual for the Fed to act once. And I think if you go back through the last many years, you're going to see a one-time cut or hike is unusual.
subtitles.zh: 回顾历史，我过去也参与过，美联储一次性行动是不寻常的。过去很多年，一次性的降息或加息很少见。

subtitles.en: Normally, these moves come in twos and threes. And so I think if you move in September, you need to be prepared there could be one or two more.
subtitles.zh: 通常这些动作是两三次连续进行。所以如果9月行动，需要准备好可能还有一两次。

subtitles.en: And that's why I think the market is saying, okay, maybe they'll have to move in September and which case they might have to do another one before March, and that's why the market's reacting that way.
subtitles.zh: 这就是为什么市场说，好吧，也许他们必须在9月行动，然后可能在3月前再来一次，所以市场这样反应。

clips.speaker_context: Goldman Sachs vice chairman and former Dallas Fed president

clips.speaker: Yvonne
clips.title: 上海交大教授：信贷放缓，增长靠创新？
title_lines: 新能源、AI能否接棒房地产？

subtitles.en: So if we do see the structural downshift in the credit impulse, where is the growth going to come from?
subtitles.zh: 如果信贷脉冲出现结构性下降，增长将从何而来？

subtitles.en: Well, I think China is trying to engineer its growth from the more debt-driven or credit-driven to the more technology or innovation-driven model.
subtitles.zh: 我认为中国正试图将增长模式从债务驱动转向技术或创新驱动。

subtitles.en: So I think it is going towards that direction. And somehow by design, I think this will require less credit and less lending from the financial institutions.
subtitles.zh: 我认为正朝着这个方向前进。某种程度上，这需要更少的信贷和金融机构贷款。

subtitles.en: So this is not necessarily a bad thing as Governor Pan pointed out. So I think we are counting more on innovation such as new energy vehicles, photovoltaics and AI.
subtitles.zh: 正如潘行长所说，这未必是坏事。我们更依赖创新，比如新能源汽车、光伏和人工智能。

subtitles.en: And high-end semiconductor innovation and I think more and more of the growth. Hopefully, we'll be coming from those areas rather than the traditional lending-intensive housing sectors.
subtitles.zh: 还有高端半导体创新，希望增长越来越多来自这些领域，而非传统的贷款密集型房地产行业。

clips.speaker_context: Finance professor at Shanghai Jiao Tong University

clips.speaker: Yvonne
clips.title: 上海交大教授：AI公司上市，市场是否低估风险？
title_lines: AI公司上市，市场低估风险？
全球流动性充裕，AI热潮能否持续？

subtitles.en: And this dovetails with what the CSRC chair talked about with the liberalizing of the rules to list these less profitable AI firms.
subtitles.zh: 这与证监会主席提到的放宽规则、允许盈利较低的AI公司上市相吻合。

subtitles.en: And we did see a surge in IPO after that, but do you think the market is maybe underpricing the risk given the lack of visibility around profits?
subtitles.zh: 此后IPO激增，但鉴于盈利前景不明，市场是否低估了风险？

subtitles.en: Well, I think we are living through a period of fairly available liquidity all over the world. So I think this is not just a China phenomenon.
subtitles.zh: 我认为我们正经历全球流动性相当充裕的时期，这并非中国独有的现象。

subtitles.en: This is probably as prevalent as it is in the NASDAQ and the US market. So I think we're going through a period of time where people have very high hope for AI and related innovation and also at the same time people are willing to pay the risk for the potential fluctuations in the market eventually.
subtitles.zh: 这与纳斯达克和美国市场一样普遍。当前人们对AI及相关创新抱有很高期望，同时愿意为市场潜在波动承担风险。

subtitles.en: So I think the jury is still out for whether we're making the right bet at the right moment.
subtitles.zh: 所以，我们是否在正确时机押对了注，尚无定论。

clips.speaker_context: Finance professor at Shanghai Jiao Tong University

clips.speaker: Yvonne
clips.title: 上海交大教授：内地与香港市场互补，公司如何选择？

subtitles.en: And is it going to come at an expense of Hong Kong because China is now encouraging Hong Kong listed firms to list in China as well? I think so.
subtitles.zh: 这是否会以香港为代价？因为中国现在也鼓励香港上市公司回内地上市？我认为是的。

subtitles.en: I think China and Hong Kong have always been playing a fairly healthy, complementary role to each other. In a way, some of the companies choose Hong Kong because Hong Kong has more flexible listing requirements and more liquidity and availability of foreign capital.
subtitles.zh: 我认为内地和香港一直扮演着相当健康、互补的角色。有些公司选择香港，因为香港上市要求更灵活，流动性更强，外资更易获得。

subtitles.en: On the other hand, I think China's mainland market enjoys a higher valuation and more liquidity. So in a way, it's a choice of the companies and the financial institutions in which market or which venue fits their needs the best.
subtitles.zh: 另一方面，内地市场估值更高、流动性更强。所以，公司和金融机构会选择最适合其需求的市场或平台。

subtitles.en: And we heard from the FX regulator as well about potentially looking into creating offshore RMB FX trading in the future.
subtitles.zh: 我们还听到外汇监管机构提到未来可能考虑建立离岸人民币外汇交易。

clips.speaker_context: Finance professor at Shanghai Jiao Tong University

clips.speaker: Yvonne
clips.title: 上海交大教授：人民币汇率改革，衍生品引入是健康一步
title_lines: 衍生品引入是健康一步

subtitles.en: I think like many reforms going on in China or has been going on in China, I think the reform is probably going to be gradual and step-by-step. So in a way, I don't think we're going to see a lot of shocks or impacts to the financial institutions or corporations at the very moment.
subtitles.zh: 我认为像中国许多正在进行的改革一样，改革可能是渐进的、一步一步的。因此，短期内不会对金融机构或企业造成很大冲击。

subtitles.en: But I think the introduction of derivatives of China's FX exchange rate trading, I think that is a very healthy step for having more market participants, joining the market, setting the price through different channels.
subtitles.zh: 但引入人民币外汇交易衍生品是非常健康的一步，可以让更多市场参与者加入，通过不同渠道定价。

subtitles.en: I think that's always a healthy and constructive direction for the further reform of exchange rate of RMB.
subtitles.zh: 我认为这对人民币汇率进一步改革始终是健康且建设性的方向。
en_highlights: reform of exchange rate of RMB

clips.speaker_context: Finance professor at Shanghai Jiao Tong University

clips.speaker: Yvonne
clips.title: 上海交大教授：离岸人民币市场创新，外资参与仍需改革

subtitles.en: And to what extent do you think this is going to draw more inflows, global inflows into the Chinese bond market, especially with the offshore RMB bond futures trading that is going to be supported by the government as well?
subtitles.zh: 这在多大程度上会吸引更多全球资金流入中国债券市场，尤其是政府支持离岸人民币债券期货交易？

subtitles.en: Yes, I think the offshore Chinese exchange rate and the offshore bond market is a very healthy whereas onshore in the free trade grounds in Shanghai, I think that's a very innovative step for China to experiment with various possible venues and platforms to trade and determine prices for both the interest rate and the exchange rate.
subtitles.zh: 是的，我认为离岸人民币汇率和离岸债券市场非常健康，而在上海自贸区，这是一个非常创新的举措，让中国尝试各种平台来交易和确定利率与汇率。

subtitles.en: That being said, I think what we probably need to see as the governor Zhu pointed out, we probably need to see more reforms in the capital accounts flow and in terms of the facilitation of the setting up of entities in the free trade zone in order for foreign players to play a more active and a more continuous role in setting the prices in those markets.
subtitles.zh: 话虽如此，正如朱行长指出，我们可能需要更多资本账户流动改革，以及便利自贸区实体设立，以便外资在这些市场定价中发挥更积极、持续的作用。
en_highlights: reforms in the capital accounts flow

subtitles.en: And is this enough do you think to encourage foreign investors for an institution to hold the RMB for the longer term? As an alternative asset and not just for purely transactional purposes? I think that is probably a different topic.
subtitles.zh: 您认为这足以鼓励外国机构长期持有人民币作为替代资产，而不仅仅是交易目的吗？我认为这可能是另一个话题。
en_highlights: hold the RMB for the longer term

clips.speaker_context: Finance professor at Shanghai Jiao Tong University

clips.speaker: Shinjuro Kozumi
clips.title: 日本防卫大臣：1%上限长期束缚防卫预算，应优先需求
title_lines: 应优先需求而非百分比

subtitles.en: And his first international TV interview, Shinjuro Kozumi, told us that Japan would be transparent about spending on new warfare methods to such as drones and AI.
subtitles.zh: 在他的首次国际电视采访中，木住晋次郎告诉我们，日本将在无人机和AI等新型作战方式的支出上保持透明。

subtitles.en: What I feel as defense minister is that because a 1% cap was securely in place for so long, we were unable to allocate funding to areas that truly needed it.
subtitles.zh: 作为防卫大臣，我的感受是，由于1%的上限长期牢固存在，我们无法将资金分配到真正需要的领域。

subtitles.en: The SDF has continuously had to endure this constraint. I want people to understand that first.
subtitles.zh: 自卫队一直不得不忍受这种制约。我希望人们首先理解这一点。

subtitles.en: If we look at what is genuinely required right now, the necessary gear and our personnel executing their duties with high morale, despite this harsh security landscape, I want to purely request what is truly needed first, rather than focusing on percentages or baseline numbers.
subtitles.zh: 如果我们看看当前真正需要什么——必要的装备和人员在严峻安全环境下保持高昂士气履行职责——我想纯粹地先请求真正需要的东西，而不是关注百分比或基准数字。

subtitles.en: What kind of figure that turns into is something to look at afterward.
subtitles.zh: 最终变成什么数字，那是之后才考虑的事情。

clips.speaker: Shinjuro Kozumi
clips.title: 日本防卫大臣：中国军费不透明引发关切

subtitles.en: Jiu Gukunol, let me ask about the increase in China's military spending. You express concern over this issue very clearly at the recent Shangri-La dialogue, which specific field causes you the strongest concern.
subtitles.zh: 久古诺尔先生，请问关于中国军费的增长。你在最近的香格里拉对话会上非常明确地表达了对此问题的关切，哪个具体领域让你最担忧？

subtitles.en: Please listen to what I say. One thing is a clear statement. One element is transparency.
subtitles.zh: 请听我说。一件事是明确的声明。一个要素是透明度。

subtitles.en: We explain our strategy with high transparency. Our budgets undergo scrutiny and deliberation in the diet and just as I am taking this interview with you, Mr. Gail.
subtitles.zh: 我们以高度透明的方式解释我们的战略。我们的预算在国会接受审查和审议，就像我现在接受你的采访一样，盖尔先生。

subtitles.en: We provide the necessary explanations domestically and internationally. Conversely, what a non-democratic nation offered this many opportunities to explain things to its legislature, and are the figures they put forward genuinely grounded in fact, backed by evidence and highly transparent?
subtitles.zh: 我们在国内和国际上提供必要的解释。相反，一个非民主国家有多少机会向其立法机构解释事情？他们提出的数字是否真正基于事实、有证据支持且高度透明？

subtitles.en: When doubts arise on these points, how much effort do they put into explaining them? It remains a reality that, despite whatever nominal figures are presented, countries hold reservations regarding that transparency.
subtitles.zh: 当对这些点产生疑问时，他们付出了多少努力来解释？现实仍然是，无论提出什么名义数字，各国对那种透明度都持保留态度。
